facts.value: next regular payday or within two weeks of termination, whichever is sooner
facts.summary: Nebraska: when an employee is fired or laid off, final wages are due next regular payday or within two weeks of termination, whichever is sooner.
facts.evidence_quote: (a) Whenever an employer, other than a political subdivision, separates an employee from the payroll, the unpaid wages shall become due on the next regular payday or within two weeks of the date of termination, whichever is sooner

facts.value: next regular payday or within two weeks of termination, whichever is sooner
facts.summary: Nebraska: when an employee is quits or resigns, final wages are due next regular payday or within two weeks of termination, whichever is sooner.
facts.evidence_quote: Nebraska law requires that final wages be paid on the next regular pay day or within two weeks of the termination, whichever is sooner. This law applies regardless of whether you are terminated or you voluntarily quit.
facts.source_title: Nebraska Department of Labor, Wage and Hour FAQ
facts.notes: Statute: Neb. Rev. Stat. 48-1230 (https://nebraskalegislature.gov/laws/statutes.php?statute=48-1230). Commissions follow 48-1230.01.

facts.applies_to: As listed by U.S. DOL, page updated November 5, 2026
facts.summary: Nebraska basic state minimum wage listed by U.S. DOL: $15.00.
facts.evidence_quote: Applicable to employers of 4 or more employees Basic Minimum Rate (per hour): $15.00
facts.source_title: State Minimum Wage Laws (U.S. DOL Wage and Hour Division)
facts.source_publisher: U.S. Department of Labor, Wage and Hour Division
facts.notes: Local (city or county) minimum wages are not included. Scheduled January 1, 2027 increases are not reflected until DOL updates the page.
